description:
Problem: building the MCP server changes process-wide state. benchbox.mcp.create_server() (benchbox/mcp/__init__.py:35-53) calls create_benchbox_server(), which turns on quiet printing (benchbox/mcp/server.py:108-110), sets the shared benchbox logger's level and adds a stderr handler when it has none (server.py:91-97, 111), installs a global OpenTelemetry tracer provider when an OTLP endpoint is configured (server.py:126; benchbox/mcp/telemetry.py:110-129, set at :124), and for remote servers adds a redaction filter to the mcp.server.transport_security logger (server.py:138; benchbox/mcp/security.py:151-154). In-process callers inherit all of it. scripts/doc_contracts.py builds two servers (:452, :478) and needs a save-and-restore wrapper that also strips OTLP variables (:396-416). Three module-scoped test fixtures leave the benchbox logger at INFO with an extra handler (tests/unit/mcp/test_mcp_low_disk_guard.py:21-31, test_mcp_statistics_phase.py:22-36, test_mcp_tool_handlers.py:21-34). On 2026-10-24 the docs-export fixture left the logger at ERROR and turned Trunk red; #3385 contained that in the exporter only. Saving and restoring globals is not a concurrency boundary.

Outcome: construction has no process-wide side effects. Process configuration happens once at the existing run_server() boundary (benchbox/mcp/__init__.py:56-92), the only production caller of create_server (:91; benchbox-mcp and python -m benchbox.mcp reach it through benchbox/mcp/cli.py:88). Stdio startup stays quiet, rejection logs on the served remote path stay redacted, and MCP tool and resource contracts are unchanged.

Callers on develop 121f24c2a: production benchbox/mcp/__init__.py:91 only; scripts/doc_contracts.py:452 and :478; tests in tests/unit/mcp (14 modules), tests/unit/landing/test_landing_quickstarts.py:272, tests/integration/mcp (_security.py:60, _transport.py:23, test_multiworker_acceptance.py:89-90, test_secret_egress.py:61 and :91), tests/integration/test_deprecation_warnings_visible.py:121, test_execution_engine_recording.py and test_execution_engine_sources.py. No docs or examples call create_server; the docs describe only the benchbox-mcp entry point (docs/reference/mcp.md, docs/guides/mcp-integration.md).

Public API status: create_server is in benchbox.mcp.__all__ but not in _project/design/api-public-symbols.json or any docs page, and docs/reference/public-contracts.md:35 covers MCP tool schemas only. Treat it as an undocumented export: record the change with a changelog.d fragment (category changed, not breaking).

Decision gates:
1. Telemetry. Today configure_telemetry does nothing without an endpoint (telemetry.py:113-114) and raises rather than replacing an existing SDK provider (:117-118). Move it into the run_server startup path so in-process construction never takes or rejects the global provider. Record the choice in the PR body. If the move changes which spans benchbox-mcp exports (tests/integration/mcp/test_observability_and_cache.py), stop and report.
2. Redaction filter. Move configure_transport_security_logging into the run_server startup path, and make tests/integration/mcp/test_secret_egress.py:77-124 build its app through that same startup step so it still proves that the served path redacts hostile Host and Origin values. If the filter cannot move without the served path losing redaction, keep it at remote construction, exclude only that filter from the unchanged-state assertions (including tests/unit/scripts/test_doc_contracts.py:150-178), and record which option was taken.
3. Stop and ask the owner if a caller outside this repository is found to depend on construction side effects, or if the change turns out to need a breaking changelog entry.

Item guardrails: stdio startup stays quiet (nothing on stdout before the JSON-RPC handshake); remote rejection logs stay redacted on the served path; telemetry exports only benchbox.mcp spans through ScopeFilteringExporter; the rendered doc contracts stay byte-identical. Rewrite, do not delete, the tests that pinned construction side effects (tests/unit/mcp/test_mcp_stdout_isolation.py:15-28 and :101-120): they move to the run_server boundary. Remove code the cutover makes dead: the exporter wrapper and OTLP stripping in scripts/doc_contracts.py, the quiet save/restore in the three module fixtures above, and the _mcp_stdio_state fixture in tests/unit/mcp/conftest.py if nothing else needs it.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits, PR bodies, docs and changelog fragments carry no tracker item IDs or session labels; any timing uses benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time().
